notes.kino: For ki- class things: kino kitabo, this book.

guidebook.intro: Uganda uses shillings, and prices quickly run into thousands. Being able to hear and say big numbers makes the market much easier.

tips.title: Building numbers
body: After ten, add with **na** (“and”): **ikumi na ibiri** is 12. Before a vowel, **na** shortens to **n’**: **ikumi n’emu** is 11.

Tens are **amakumi** plus a number: **amakumi abiri** (20), **amakumi asatu** (30). Hundreds are **kikumi** and **bikumi**, thousands **lukumi** and **nkumi**, and ten thousand has its own word, **omutwalo**.

culture.title: Haggling is expected
body: At markets and with boda boda riders, the first price is an opening offer. Smile, say **Kendeezaako**, and meet somewhere in the middle. Supermarkets and shops with price tags are fixed.

culture.title: Shillings
body: Common notes are 1,000, 2,000, 5,000, 10,000, 20,000 and 50,000 shillings, and coins go down to 50. People often say just the number: **nkumi ibiri** means 2,000 shillings.
